name: 10X GENOMICS, INC.
agency: Department of Health and Human Services
brief_text:
Three detectors fired for 10X Genomics. Benford's Law analysis found a significant deviation in the leading-digit distribution of award amounts, with digit 2 appearing far more frequently than expected and digit 1 appearing less frequently. A parent contract modification grew at a rate 164.5 times its initial value, roughly 15 times faster than peers in biological product manufacturing. An Isolation Forest multivariate analysis flagged the entity as a statistical outlier based on its combination of award volume, agency concentration, and modification patterns.

The Benford test yielded a Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic of 0.290 with p-value 3.4e-24 across 326 transactions. The worst-performing contract (75N98022A00032) showed a modification growth ratio of 164.5 versus a NAICS average of 11.1, producing a z-score of 5.45. The Isolation Forest score of 0.883 reflects an entity with 326 awards across only 2 agencies, 13 NAICS codes, and a competition ratio of 0.006, indicating heavy sole-source concentration.

These statistical anomalies warrant scrutiny but do not confirm fraud. Benford deviations can arise from legitimate clustering of contract values in certain ranges. The modification growth spike may reflect a large, multi-year research program with staged funding rather than improper cost escalation. The entity's narrow agency footprint and high modification frequency are consistent with a specialized biotech vendor serving HHS repeatedly. The small peer group in this NAICS code limits the robustness of comparative benchmarks.
